notes.title: Update - Pathfinding Improvements
notes.notes:
Long time no see! We've had a huge break from writing news, but the game development didn't stop even for a moment in that time. Actually, there's been a lot of exciting things happening behind the scenes.

Anyway, today it's time to talk about Pathfinding in Liquidation.

There've been some significant updates recently, and it's time to share them with the community! 
To start the topic, here's a dev view of how buildings can now look on the pathfinding grid in Liquidation:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/47e3c4ac391e284316b48f84bc30b60f566f453a.png[/img]

It's important to note that before this round of changes, the buildings were simple rectangles on the pathfinding grid. Now, the shapes on the grid match the actual buildings much better.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/5c0a0443a65edc40a861949168fc53d2e2bc103a.png[/img]

The consequence of them being simple rectangles was as simple as the following picture present. The units weren't able to sneak through corners. But now, after the change - they can. 
[i]That also means Dominus can finally walk between the two buildings and deal decisive blows to anyone who dares to oppose the Twilight Crusade![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/471769fdf5ca6a8d2096e2ad448c7d5bd804e352.png[/img]

Now that we've got that out of the way - let's move on to the meat of this news post.

You might remember from the news about [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/896250/view/7950611950253970692]Corrupt Nether Environment[/url] that idle avoidance response got improved in Liquidation. That was another one of the steps towards what's shown below. 

Using other avoidance behaviors, Local Avoidance introduction improved unit behavior around buildings. 
After that, and a few updates later, we've arrived at the results you can inspect on the video here:

[i]The Corruption raids a Twilight Crusade outpost, who's going to win this battle? Will it influence the war efforts?[/i] 
[previewyoutube=nauYBTG7YiM;full][/previewyoutube]

Please share your thoughts! 
Maybe you want to ask a question about the Corruption appearance in this news post? Ask away!

------

notes.title: Weekly Update - Translations
notes.notes:
This week, we're ready to announce that Liquidation now supports community translations! We will be looking for people to help with translations in the future, so keep your eyes peeled for further news, as this is a community-driven effort!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/ab116575b836bfe16c6ecef45d184a883804bd14.png[/img]

For starters, we ran an automatic translation to the Korean language. Next, we invited the community to begin translating the game to Spanish and Polish languages. The system seems to work, which bodes well for the future. We're still testing and uncovering bugs. 
The screenshots you can see here present some elements of the Polish translation of the game. There are still some kinks to be worked out with the fonts, but nothing we can't accomplish over time.

One of the features that we want to keep in the game is switching between languages in the game on the fly. You can change the language in the settings even during a match. Currently, we're testing English, German, Polish, Spanish, and Korean texts, as it seems people speaking those languages are waiting for the game the most, according to our Wishlist data.
Incomplete translations will have their missing texts keep the English versions. 

Please let us know what languages you'd like to see next for the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/bf5db1c817d2371db82a322db43da65acdf389fc.png[/img]

notes.title: Weekly Update - Corrupted Nether Environment
notes.notes:
In the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/896250/announcements/detail/4024598238779766416]news last week[/url] we announced the Legion faction is almost finished. There, you might've learned that the Nether started to consume the fabrics of reality, and now it's reflected in the corrupted Nether environment.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/315fd5138e49de031e35ef147df6a2122f8663e0.png[/img]

This change should allow the world to be much more filled, which is one of the most important things to address before Liquidation is ready for Early Access. 

Which part of this environment do you like the most? What's the thing you'd like to see next? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/de1a2fe8216e6d812eb56815ad015974587f089e.png[/img]

We've also improved the idle avoidance response, but what does that mean? 
While playing RTS games, you might've noticed that units need to interact with each other when not directly controlled - for example - when a group of your units is passing through your idle army.
After introducing unit collision a while back, we faced a problem - idle units often blocked moving ones... So here's a demo of how it works now, where Husks - Legion faction workers - are running around other Husks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38134458/aaf4e741ac086a1487959e70302a43dae0a5a1b6.gif[/img]

notes.title: Weekly Update - Big news for competetive community!
notes.notes:
Another weekly update is here! Granted, I might have missed the last 30 or 40 weekly updates. But this one is worth the silence! At least, I hope. 

The big (semi-big?) news is that we now have working replay functionality! Not only that, but our replays are very small and thus easy to share! This way, I am hoping to boost community sharing of replays and reviewing various matches to improve yourself or to see if the other guy cheated or not. (So far 0 cheaters have been detected though) 

Enjoy this little mundane game - that might not been exciting to watch - but proves the replay functionality!

[previewyoutube=bpVtIcOAYNU;full][/previewyoutube]
